chunks: Aḥmad ibn Rizq al-Ghumshānī narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام instructed me to press his abdomen, then perform wudu (ablution) for him, then wash him with ushnaan, then wash his head with sidr and his beard, then pour some of it over his body, then rub his body with it, then pour over him three times, then wash him with pure water, then pour over him water with camphor and with pure water, and place in it seven leaves of sidr.

key_terms.أُوَضِّئَهُ: to perform wudu (ablution) for him before the washing
key_terms.السِّدْرِ: lote leaves used in ritual washing
key_terms.الْأُشْنَانِ: a cleansing substance used in washing the body
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor used in the washing of the deceased
key_terms.جَسَدِهِ: his body, referring to the deceased being washed
key_terms.سَبْعَ وَرَقَاتِ سِدْرٍ: seven leaves of sidr placed in the water

ai.seo_question: How is the deceased to be washed according to a hadith from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a detailed procedure taught by Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام for the ritual washing of the deceased. It outlines the sequence of cleansing materials and actions used in preparing the body, reflecting the fiqh of funerary taharah in Shia tradition.
